evidence: Engraving is the same: nasta'liq «انك على كل شيء قدير» inside a scalloped cartouche, with the five-petal flowers in the same places (a cluster above شيء, single flowers inside the bowls, a small mark under شيء). The darker patch at the left of the stone also matches. Mount agrees too: beaded bezel, quilted (grid) shoulders, plain shank. Compared v02 f005/f006/f013 with #84 (front), #82, #83 (side) and #85 (F hallmark with two round stamps). The metal looks gold in #82-85 only because of the warm lighting of the 2021 shoot.
candidates_rejected: g2-24 (#331/#332/#333): the other ring the describer read as «…على كل شيء قدير». It is a pale green-grey translucent stone with a different nasta'liq layout, on a vertically fluted shank with beaded rims; v02 has an orange carnelian with quilted shoulders. g1-48 (#209) and g1-52 (#226): nasta'liq carnelians with different text and knurled or grooved shoulders. g4-12 (#628): different text, striped shank. g3-26 (#531): diagonal layout.

evidence: Thuluth «سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا اله الا الله والله اكبر» with an identical layout: two registers divided by a long diagonal stroke, the same small flowers and the same line ends. Stone is the same milky grey agate with a brownish underside. Mount is the same unusual openwork of teardrop loops all around the bezel, with a broad shank and a fine beaded line. Compared f003/f005/f006 with #1019 (front) and #1020 (side). Hallmark #1021. Owner code R003.
candidates_rejected: g5-44 (#985): white agate, 2-line text, heavy vertical ribs. g5-45 (#989): small milky stone, short text. g6-19 (#1114): fully fluted mount, «لا اله الا الله الملك الحق المبين». g2-28 (#350) and g3-27 (#535): different text and mounts.

evidence: The mount is the same model. An oval sky-blue turquoise without matrix sits in 4 claws. Shoulders are fan-ribbed and end in a beaded band before the plain shank. Small heart-shaped cut-outs with gold-tone inserts sit above and below the bezel, and there is a small V-pattern between the upper hearts. Stone colour and shape also agree. Compared f004/f005/f009/f022 with #1080 (front), #1081 (side) and #1082 (F hallmark with two round stamps). Not high because the stone is unengraved with no visible marks to confirm. The video also shows darker, oxidised ribs than the polished ring in #1080/#1081, so it could be a sister ring of the same design.
candidates_rejected: g1-10 (#39-42): same family but yellow metal and pierced teardrop/scroll shoulders, no fan ribs. g6-06 (#1052): crown bezel on a plain shank. g6-11 (#1075): knurled shoulders. g5-24 (#899) and g2-41 (#418): spiderweb turquoise. g1-32, g2-32, g4-02, g4-04: angular or crown mounts. g5-20 and g3-39: fluted claw or knurled mounts.

evidence: The stone is the same type: an oval, bright green jadeite cabochon. The mount is the same distinctive one: petal claws (two at the top), faceted flame-like petals on the shoulders, and a beaded band where they meet the plain shank. The hallmarks visible inside the shank in f017-f019 (round stamp, F, round stamp) are laid out like those in #1346. The darker central zone of the stone in f005 fits the dark central band in #1342. Compared f004/f005/f023 with #1342 and #1344. Not high: the stone is unengraved, glare in the video hides its pattern, and the 2024 photos show tarnished metal. Owner code R005 (also filed in RS).

evidence: Domed agate split half white / half red, lightly carved «يا الله». The tall alif/lam strokes fall in the white half, cross-hatched lobed panels in the red half, and a hatched strip runs down one side. With #77 rotated 90°, the layout is the same. Mount agrees: claw bezel, deeply fluted (gadrooned) shoulders ending in a beaded band, plain shank. Compared f004/f022/f023 with #77 and #76, hallmark #78. Gold colour in #76-78 is the warm lighting of the 2021 shoot.
